FROM php:8.3-bookworm

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    git ca-certificates curl mariadb-server=1:10.11.18-0+deb12u1 mariadb-client=1:10.11.18-0+deb12u1 \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN docker-php-ext-install pdo_mysql

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs npm \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN mkdir -p /opt/verifier-deps \
 && cd /opt/verifier-deps \
 && npm init -y >/dev/null \
 && npm install --no-audit --no-fund playwright@1.48.2 \
 && npx --yes playwright@1.48.2 install --with-deps chromium
ENV NODE_PATH=/opt/verifier-deps/node_modules

RUN { \
      echo 'pdo_mysql.default_socket=/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock'; \
      echo 'mysqli.default_socket=/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock'; \
    } > /usr/local/etc/php/conf.d/zzz-mysql-socket.ini

WORKDIR /app

RUN git clone https://github.com/MR-VL/Consolidev /app \
 && git -C /app checkout 41756ef8acc7d759d0204f058055e4adf1948fdf \
 && ln -s Database.php /app/database.php \
 && ln -s Header.php /app/header.php \
 && ln -s Header.js /app/header.js \
 && rm -rf /app/.git \
 && git -C /app init -q \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h add -A \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h commit -q -m base \
 && git -C /app tag harbor_base

RUN mkdir -p /var/run/mysqld && chown -R mysql:mysql /var/run/mysqld /var/lib/mysql \
 && mariadb-install-db --user=root --datadir=/var/lib/mysql --auth-root-authentication-method=normal >/dev/null \
 && (mysqld --user=root --datadir=/var/lib/mysql --socket=/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock &) \
 && for i in $(seq 1 60); do mysqladmin ping --socket=/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 1; done \
 && mysqladmin ping --socket=/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock >/dev/null 2>&1 \
 && mysql -uroot --socket=/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock -e "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS consolidev;" \
 && sed 's/utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci/utf8mb4_unicode_ci/g' /app/SQL_DUMP/consolidev.sql | mysql -uroot --socket=/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock consolidev \
 && mysqladmin -uroot --socket=/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock shutdown \
 && sleep 2

RUN { \
      echo '#!/usr/bin/env bash'; \
      echo 'set -e'; \
      echo 'mkdir -p /var/run/mysqld && chown mysql:mysql /var/run/mysqld'; \
      echo 'mysqld --user=root --datadir=/var/lib/mysql --socket=/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock &'; \
      echo 'for i in $(seq 1 60); do mysqladmin ping --socket=/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 1; done'; \
      echo 'php -S 0.0.0.0:18080 -t /app >/logs/php.log 2>&1 &'; \
      echo 'for i in $(seq 1 30); do curl -fsS -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:18080/login.php && break; sleep 1; done'; \
    } > /usr/local/bin/start_services.sh \
 && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/start_services.sh

RUN mkdir -p /logs /app/.harbor_assets
COPY assets/ /app/.harbor_assets/

CMD ["bash"]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse
import atexit
import json
import os
import sys

CONF = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
F2P = CONF['f2p']
P2P = CONF['p2p']
REPORT = '/logs/verifier/measure.json'

_CANON_JSON = "/logs/verifier/reward.json"
_CANON_TXT = "/logs/verifier/reward.txt"
_canon = {}

def canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric,
                 f2p_detail=None, p2p_detail=None):
    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)
    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)
    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q
    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
    _canon.clear()
    _canon.update({
        "reward": 0.0 if rubric == "fail" else tests_passed,
        "tests_passed": tests_passed,
        "f2p_passed": f, "f2p_total": t,
        "p2p_passed": p, "p2p_total": q,
        "rubric_passed": {"pass": 1, "fail": 0}.get(rubric, -1),
    })
    # Per-test outcomes, alongside the canonical seven (QC strips `::` keys before validating
    # the schema, so these are an expected extra rather than a violation).
    #
    # The aggregate counts cannot say WHICH test passed, so an f2p test that also passes on an
    # empty submission -- an inert test that can never detect the bug -- is invisible in
    # f2p_passed/f2p_total. QC reads these off the Nop run to catch exactly that. With a single
    # f2p test the aggregate happens to be equivalent; with more than one it is not.
    for prefix, detail in (("f2p", f2p_detail or {}), ("p2p", p2p_detail or {})):
        for ident, outcome in detail.items():
            _canon["%s::%s" % (prefix, ident)] = 1.0 if outcome == "pass" else 0.0
    return _canon["reward"]

@atexit.register
def _canon_flush():
    if not _canon:
        return
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_CANON_JSON), exist_ok=True)
        with open(_CANON_JSON, "w") as _h:
            json.dump(_canon, _h, indent=2)
        with open(_CANON_TXT, "w") as _h:
            _h.write(str(_canon["reward"]))
    except Exception as _exc:
        print("WARNING: could not write %s: %s" % (_CANON_JSON, _exc), file=sys.stderr)

def load_results():
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        return {}
    try:
        data = json.load(open(REPORT))
    except Exception:
        return {}
    results = data.get('results', {})
    return {k: ('pass' if v else 'fail') for k, v in results.items()}

def matched(idents, results):
    return {ident: results.get(ident, 'missing') for ident in idents}

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('--rubric', default='', help='"pass" | "fail" | "" (not graded)')
    args = ap.parse_args()
    rubric = (args.rubric or '').strip().lower()
    if rubric not in ('pass', 'fail'):
        rubric = None

    results = load_results()
    f2p = matched(F2P, results)
    p2p = matched(P2P, results)
    f2p_pass = [k for k, v in f2p.items() if v == 'pass']
    p2p_pass = [k for k, v in p2p.items() if v == 'pass']

    reward = canon_reward(len(f2p_pass), len(F2P),
                          len(p2p_pass), len(P2P),
                          rubric,
                          f2p_detail=f2p, p2p_detail=p2p)

    detail = {'reward': reward, 'rubric': rubric, 'f2p': f2p, 'p2p': p2p}
    os.makedirs('/logs/verifier', exist_ok=True)
    with open('/logs/verifier/reward_detail.json', 'w') as f:
        json.dump(detail, f, indent=2)
    print(json.dumps(detail))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

22	
23	          [verifier]
24	          network_mode = "public"
25	
26	      The agent phase stays closed; its model host is injected at run time instead.
27	
28	      Any failure here -- unset key, blocked egress, HTTP error, unparseable response --
29	      falls through to the sub-agent request below. The judge must never fail the run.
30	
31	  Sub-agent (fallback, out-of-band)
32	
33	  Phase 1 (during the verifier run)
34	      No verdict exists yet, so this writes a self-contained judge request into the judge
35	      dir -- criteria_payload.json, source.txt (the candidate diff), changed_files.txt (the
36	      FULL text of every file the diff touched), and PROMPT.md -- prints nothing, and exits 0.
37	      The verifier then scores on tests alone.
38	
39	      What the judge deliberately does NOT get: the task instruction (a criterion that has to
40	      defer to the prompt is a Major "not self-contained" rubric defect -- handing the judge the
41	      prompt would let such a criterion pass and hide the defect), the golden solution/fix.patch
42	      (seeing it turns
43	      the judge into a similarity checker, reintroducing the very overfitting the rubric exists
44	      to catch), the tests/test.patch (same failure mode, and the tests already score that),
45	      the before/after images (UI-evaluation criteria are out of scope by definition), and
46	      browse access to the wider repo (unavailable at rescore time, so it would work in phase 1
47	      and silently not in phase 2).
48	
49	  Phase 2 (after the run, orchestrated outside the container)
50	      A judge sub-agent reads PROMPT.md and writes verdict.json next to it. Re-running this
51	      script (or `mm_run.sh <task> rescore`) reads that verdict and prints "pass" or "fail".
52	
53	Contract (test.sh and verifier.py depend on all four):
54	  * prints "pass" or "fail" on stdout, or NOTHING when no verdict is available yet.
55	    stdout is captured verbatim into test.sh's RUBRIC, so every diagnostic goes to stderr.
56	  * writes the per-criterion detail to <judge dir>/summary.json
57	  * writes {"failed": [...]} to /logs/verifier/rubric.json, which is the path verifier.py
58	    actually reads for rubric_failed_count (it previously only ever found summary.json in
59	    the judge dir, so that count was structurally always 0)
60	  * ALWAYS exits 0, so the judge can never fail the run
61	
62	Env:
63	  EVAL_API_KEY      LiteLLM proxy key; absent => skip the API backend entirely
64	  EVAL_BASE_URL     OpenAI-compatible base, already ending in /v1
65	  EVAL_MODEL        model name as registered on the proxy
66	  EVAL_USER         optional; sent as the request's `user` so the proxy can attribute spend
67	  PB_JUDGE_DIR      where the request/verdict live (default /logs/verifier/judge)
68	  PB_JUDGE_VERDICT  explicit path to verdict.json (overrides the default location)
69	
70	Only the stdlib is used for the HTTP call: the verifier image is node:22-bookworm with no
71	pip install step, so requests/httpx are not available.
72	
73	IMPORTANT: never name a file in tests/ after a stdlib module (select.py, json.py, types.py,
74	io.py, queue.py). It shadows the real module and the failure surfaces somewhere unrelated.
75	The sys.path strip below defends against it.

101	EXCLUDE_RE = re.compile(
102	    # Widened beyond the original JS/TS-only patterns. Measured against the corpus, the

128	def mark_untracked(repo: str) -> None:
129	    """Make files the submission ADDED visible to `git diff`.
130	
131	    `git diff <ref>` reports tracked paths only, so a fix delivered as a NEW file -- a new
132	    stylesheet, a new module -- does not appear in it at all. The judge would then grade
133	    criteria about that file having never seen its contents and, under the "score 0 when
134	    unsure" rule, fail a correct submission. Observed on this task: the golden fix adds
135	    CSS/jwtHistory.css carrying every layout rule, and the two criteria that read it scored
136	    0 while the one criterion satisfiable from the tracked file alone scored 1.
137	
138	    `add -N` (intent-to-add) records the paths in the index WITHOUT staging content, which
139	    is the smallest change that makes them show up as additions in the diff. Untracked
140	    paths that .gitignore covers stay hidden, which is what we want for build artefacts.
141	    """
142	    try:
143	        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard"],
144	                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
145	        paths = [p for p in (out.stdout or "").splitlines() if p.strip()]
146	        if not paths:
147	            return
148	        add = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "add", "-N"] + paths,
149	                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
150	        if add.returncode == 0:
151	            sys.stderr.write("[judge] marked %d added file(s) intent-to-add so the diff "
152	                             "shows them: %s\n" % (len(paths), ", ".join(paths[:10])))
153	        else:
154	            sys.stderr.write("[judge] git add -N exited %d: %s\n"
155	                             % (add.returncode, (add.stderr or "").strip()[:300]))
156	    except Exception as exc:
157	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] could not mark untracked files: %s\n" % exc)

160	def candidate_diff(repo: str, budget: int = 120_000) -> str:
161	    mark_untracked(repo)
162	    for ref in BASE_REFS:
163	        try:
164	            out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "diff", ref],
165	                                 capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
166	        except Exception as exc:
167	            sys.stderr.write("[judge] git diff failed: %s\n" % exc)
168	            return ""
169	        if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
170	            sys.stderr.write("[judge] diffing against %s\n" % ref)
171	            return filter_diff(out.stdout, budget)
172	        # Surface WHY a ref produced nothing. A non-zero git exit here (bad ref, dubious
173	        # ownership, corrupt index) is indistinguishable from "the agent changed nothing"
174	        # unless we say so, and it silently skips rubric grading entirely.
175	        if out.returncode != 0:
176	            sys.stderr.write(
177	                "[judge] git diff %s exited %d: %s\n"
178	                % (ref, out.returncode, (out.stderr or "").strip()[:300])
179	            )
180	    sys.stderr.write("[judge] no non-empty diff found against any of %s\n"
181	                     % ", ".join(BASE_REFS))
182	    return ""

185	def filter_diff(diff: str, budget: int) -> str:
186	    kept, cur, keep = [], [], True
187	    for line in diff.splitlines(keepends=True):
188	        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
189	            if keep and cur:
190	                kept.extend(cur)
191	            parts = line.split()
192	            path = parts[-1][2:] if len(parts) >= 4 else ""
193	            keep = not EXCLUDE_RE.search(path)
194	            cur = [line]
195	        else:
196	            cur.append(line)
197	    if keep and cur:
198	        kept.extend(cur)
199	    blob = "".join(kept)
200	    return blob[:budget] + "\n[... truncated ...]\n" if len(blob) > budget else blob
201

203	def changed_paths(diff: str) -> list:
204	    """Paths touched by the (already harness-filtered) diff, in order."""
205	    out = []
206	    for line in diff.splitlines():
207	        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
208	            parts = line.split()
209	            if len(parts) >= 4:
210	                p = parts[-1][2:]                  # strip the b/ prefix
211	                if p and p not in out:
212	                    out.append(p)
213	    return out

216	def collect_changed_files(repo: str, diff: str, budget: int = 200_000) -> str:
217	    """Full current text of every file the diff touched.
218	
219	    A hunk shows three lines of context, which is often too little to decide a criterion that
220	    is genuinely true of the change (e.g. "the helper is defined in the same module"). Whole
221	    files remove that class of false 0 while staying bounded by the size of the change.
222	    """
223	    blob, used = [], 0
224	    for rel in changed_paths(diff):
225	        fp = Path(repo) / rel
226	        if not fp.is_file():                       # deleted or renamed away
227	            continue
228	        try:
229	            text = fp.read_text(errors="replace")
230	        except Exception:
231	            continue
232	        chunk = "\n===== %s =====\n%s" % (rel, text)
233	        if used + len(chunk) > budget:
234	            blob.append("\n[... remaining changed files omitted for length ...]\n")
235	            break
236	        blob.append(chunk); used += len(chunk)
237	    return "".join(blob)

240	def write_request(criteria, diff, jdir: Path, changed: str = "") -> None:
241	    """Lay down everything a judge sub-agent needs, with no further context."""
242	    jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
243	    payload = [{"id": c["id"], "criterion": c["criterion"]} for c in criteria]
244	    (jdir / "criteria_payload.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
245	    (jdir / "source.txt").write_text(diff)
246	    extra = []
247	    if changed.strip():
248	        (jdir / "changed_files.txt").write_text(changed)
249	        extra.append("- `changed_files.txt` — the FULL current text of every file the diff "
250	                     "touched. Use it when a hunk alone is too little context to decide a "
251	                     "criterion.")
252	    extra_block = ("\n" + "\n".join(extra)) if extra else ""
253	    verdict = jdir / "verdict.json"
254	    ids = ", ".join(c["id"] for c in criteria)
255	    (jdir / "PROMPT.md").write_text(f"""# Rubric judge (sub-agent)
256	
257	You are the rubric judge. Grade the APPROACH of a code change, not whether its tests pass.
258	
259	System contract:
260	{JUDGE_SYSTEM}
261	
262	Inputs in this directory ({jdir}):
263	- `criteria_payload.json` — {len(criteria)} criteria, each {{id, criterion}}.
264	- `source.txt` — the candidate diff. Test, spec and snapshot files are already stripped out,
265	  so everything you see is product code the submission changed.{extra_block}
266	
267	You are NOT given the task instruction, the reference/golden fix, the tests, or the rest of the
268	repository. Judge only what is here. If a criterion cannot be decided from these inputs, score it 0 — but note that a
269	criterion which is undecidable here is a defect in the rubric, not in the submission.
270	
271	Score each criterion **1 or 0 — never 0.5 or any fraction**. 1 = fully satisfied,
272	0 = not satisfied, ambiguous, or no clear evidence. Be strict; when unsure, score 0.
273	
274	The rubric is unweighted and every criterion is mandatory: a single 0 fails the whole rubric,
275	so do not withhold a 1 over style preferences the criterion does not actually state.
276	
277	Write ONLY this JSON to `{verdict}`:
278	
279	    {{"scores": {{"<criterion id>": {{"score": 0|1}}, ...}}}}
280	
281	All {len(criteria)} ids must appear: {ids}. Verify the file parses before you finish.
282	""")
283	
284	
285	def build_user_prompt(criteria, diff: str, changed: str) -> str:
286	    """The API-backend counterpart of PROMPT.md, with the same inputs and exclusions.
287	
288	    Deliberately withheld, exactly as in the sub-agent request: the task instruction, the
289	    golden fix.patch, tests/test.patch, and the screenshots. See the module docstring for
290	    why each one would corrupt the grade.
291	    """
292	    payload = json.dumps(
293	        [{"id": c["id"], "criterion": c["criterion"]} for c in criteria], indent=2
294	    )
295	    ids = ", ".join(c["id"] for c in criteria)
296	    parts = [
297	        "Grade the APPROACH of the code change below against each rubric criterion.",
298	        "",
299	        "## Criteria",
300	        payload,
301	        "",
302	        "## Candidate diff (test/spec/snapshot files already stripped)",
303	        "```diff",
304	        diff,
305	        "```",
306	    ]
307	    if changed.strip():
308	        parts += [
309	            "",
310	            "## Full current text of every file the diff touched",
311	            "Use this when a hunk alone is too little context to decide a criterion.",
312	            changed,
313	        ]
314	    parts += [
315	        "",
316	        "## Output",
317	        'Reply with JSON only, no prose and no code fences: {"scores": {"<id>": 0 or 1}}.',
318	        f"All {len(criteria)} ids must be present: {ids}.",
319	        "Score 1 only when the criterion is fully satisfied with clear evidence in the "
320	        "change; otherwise score 0. There is no partial credit.",
321	    ]
322	    return "\n".join(parts)
323

325	def extract_scores_object(text: str):
326	    """Parse the model reply into a dict, tolerating fences and surrounding prose."""
327	    candidate = text.strip()
328	    if candidate.startswith("```"):
329	        candidate = re.sub(r"^```[a-zA-Z]*\n?", "", candidate)
330	        candidate = re.sub(r"\n?```$", "", candidate.strip())
331	    try:
332	        return json.loads(candidate)
333	    except Exception:
334	        pass
335	    start, depth = None, 0
336	    for i, ch in enumerate(candidate):
337	        if ch == "{":
338	            if start is None:
339	                start = i
340	            depth += 1
341	        elif ch == "}" and start is not None:
342	            depth -= 1
343	            if depth == 0:
344	                try:
345	                    return json.loads(candidate[start : i + 1])
346	                except Exception:
347	                    start, depth = None, 0
348	    return None

351	def call_eval_api(criteria, diff: str, changed: str):
352	    """Grade via the proxy. Returns a scores-shaped dict, or None to fall back.
353	
354	    Never raises: every failure path returns None so the caller can fall through to the
355	    sub-agent request and the run is never failed by the judge.
356	    """
357	    api_key = (os.environ.get("EVAL_API_KEY") or "").strip()
358	    base_url = (os.environ.get("EVAL_BASE_URL") or "").strip().rstrip("/")
359	    model = (os.environ.get("EVAL_MODEL") or "").strip()
360	    if not api_key or not base_url or not model:
361	        sys.stderr.write(
362	            "[judge] API backend unavailable (EVAL_API_KEY/EVAL_BASE_URL/EVAL_MODEL "
363	            "incomplete); falling back to the sub-agent request\n"
364	        )
365	        return None
366	
367	    body = {
368	        "model": model,
369	        "temperature": 0,
370	        "messages": [
371	            {"role": "system", "content": JUDGE_SYSTEM},
372	            {"role": "user", "content": build_user_prompt(criteria, diff, changed)},
373	        ],
374	    }
375	    # The proxy attributes spend per `user`; without it this call is unattributable.
376	    if os.environ.get("EVAL_USER"):
377	        body["user"] = os.environ["EVAL_USER"]
378	
379	    url = base_url + "/chat/completions"
380	    data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
381	    for attempt in range(1, API_ATTEMPTS + 1):
382	        try:
383	            req = urllib.request.Request(
384	                url,
385	                data=data,
386	                method="POST",
387	                headers={
388	                    "Authorization": "Bearer %s" % api_key,
389	                    "Content-Type": "application/json",
390	                },
391	            )
392	            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=API_TIMEOUT_SEC) as resp:
393	                raw = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
394	            content = json.loads(raw)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
395	            obj = extract_scores_object(content)
396	            if not isinstance(obj, dict):
397	                sys.stderr.write(
398	                    "[judge] attempt %d: reply was not JSON: %r\n" % (attempt, content[:400])
399	                )
400	            else:
401	                sys.stderr.write("[judge] graded via API model=%s\n" % model)
402	                return obj
403	        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
404	            detail = ""
405	            try:
406	                detail = exc.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")[:400]
407	            except Exception:
408	                pass
409	            sys.stderr.write(
410	                "[judge] attempt %d: HTTP %s %s\n" % (attempt, exc.code, detail)
411	            )
412	            # 4xx other than 429 will not fix themselves; stop retrying.
413	            if 400 <= exc.code < 500 and exc.code != 429:
414	                break
415	        except Exception as exc:
416	            sys.stderr.write(
417	                "[judge] attempt %d: %s: %s\n" % (attempt, exc.__class__.__name__, exc)
418	            )
419	        if attempt < API_ATTEMPTS:
420	            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
421	    sys.stderr.write("[judge] API backend gave up; falling back to the sub-agent request\n")
422	    return None
423

425	def write_rubric_json(failed, total: int) -> None:
426	    """verifier.py reads this for rubric_failed_count."""
427	    try:
428	        Path(RUBRIC_JSON_PATH).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
429	        with open(RUBRIC_JSON_PATH, "w") as handle:
430	            json.dump({"failed": list(failed), "criteria_total": total}, handle, indent=2)
431	    except OSError as exc:
432	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] could not write %s: %s\n" % (RUBRIC_JSON_PATH, exc))
433	
434	
435	def read_verdict(criteria, jdir: Path):
436	    """Return ("pass"|"fail", failed_ids) or None when no usable verdict exists."""
437	    vp = Path(os.environ.get("PB_JUDGE_VERDICT") or (jdir / "verdict.json"))
438	    if not vp.is_file():
439	        return None
440	    try:
441	        obj = json.loads(vp.read_text())
442	    except Exception as exc:
443	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict unreadable (%s)\n" % exc)
444	        return None
445	    scores = obj.get("scores", obj)
446	    if not isinstance(scores, dict):
447	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict has no scores map\n")
448	        return None
449	    failed, graded = [], 0
450	    for c in criteria:
451	        raw = scores.get(c["id"])
452	        if raw is None:
453	            failed.append(c["id"])            # not graded == not demonstrated == fail
454	            continue
455	        try:
456	            v = float(raw.get("score") if isinstance(raw, dict) else raw)
457	        except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
458	            failed.append(c["id"])
459	            continue
460	        graded += 1
461	        if v < 1.0:                            # strictly binary: only a full 1 passes
462	            failed.append(c["id"])
463	    if graded == 0:
464	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict contained no usable scores\n")
465	        return None
466	    return ("fail" if failed else "pass"), failed
467	
468	
469	def main() -> int:
470	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
471	    ap.add_argument("--rubrics", required=True)
472	    ap.add_argument("--repo", default="/app")
473	    ap.add_argument("--judge-dir", default=None)
474	    a = ap.parse_args()
475	
476	    jdir = Path(a.judge_dir) if a.judge_dir else judge_dir()
477	    try:
478	        doc = json.load(open(a.rubrics))
479	    except Exception as exc:
480	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] cannot read %s: %s\n" % (a.rubrics, exc))
481	        return 0
482	    criteria = [c for c in (doc.get("criteria") or []) if c.get("id") and c.get("criterion")]
483	    if not criteria:
484	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] no criteria in %s\n" % a.rubrics)
485	        return 0
486	
487	    def emit(verdict, failed) -> int:
488	        """Publish a verdict: summary.json, rubric.json, then stdout LAST."""
489	        try:
490	            jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
491	            json.dump({"rubric": verdict, "failed": failed,
492	                       "criteria_total": len(criteria)},
493	                      open(jdir / "summary.json", "w"), indent=2)
494	        except Exception:
495	            pass
496	        write_rubric_json(failed, len(criteria))
497	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict=%s%s\n"
498	                         % (verdict, (" failed=%s" % ", ".join(failed)) if failed else ""))
499	        print(verdict)
500	        return 0
501	
502	    # An existing verdict.json always wins: it is either a sub-agent verdict or this
503	    # script's own API result being rescored, and re-grading would cost a second call.
504	    res = read_verdict(criteria, jdir)
505	    if res is not None:
506	        return emit(*res)
507	
508	    diff = candidate_diff(a.repo)
509	    if not diff.strip():
510	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] empty candidate diff; nothing to grade\n")
511	        return 0
512	    changed = collect_changed_files(a.repo, diff)
513	
514	    # Preferred: grade in-band via the proxy. Persist the scores as verdict.json so the
515	    # grade is auditable and a rescore is idempotent, then score it through read_verdict
516	    # so both backends share one scoring path.
517	    scores = call_eval_api(criteria, diff, changed)
518	    if scores is not None:
519	        try:
520	            jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
521	            (jdir / "verdict.json").write_text(json.dumps(scores, indent=2))
522	        except OSError as exc:
523	            sys.stderr.write("[judge] could not persist verdict.json: %s\n" % exc)
524	        res = read_verdict(criteria, jdir)
525	        if res is not None:
526	            return emit(*res)
527	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] API verdict had no usable scores; writing the request\n")
528	
529	    # Fallback: lay down the sub-agent request and stay silent.
530	    write_request(criteria, diff, jdir, changed=changed)
531	    sys.stderr.write(
532	        "[judge] no verdict at %s yet; wrote the judge request to %s (%s). Have the judge "
533	        "sub-agent produce verdict.json, then rescore. Scoring on tests alone until then.\n"
534	        % (jdir / "verdict.json", jdir, ", ".join(sorted(f.name for f in jdir.iterdir()))))
535	    return 0
536	
537	
538	if __name__ == "__main__":
539	    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Rubric judge — API backend, with the sub-agent backend as fallback.

Binary and unweighted: every criterion is PASS/FAIL and every one is mandatory, so the
rubric passes only if all pass.

Backend selection, in order:

  API (preferred, in-band)
      When EVAL_API_KEY and EVAL_BASE_URL are set, grade the criteria in one
      chat-completions call to the LiteLLM proxy, write the resulting scores map to
      verdict.json in the judge dir, then score it through the SAME read_verdict path the
      sub-agent backend uses -- so the binary / all-mandatory / "not graded == fail"
      semantics are identical whichever backend produced the verdict.

      Requires verifier-phase egress to whatever EVAL_BASE_URL points at. Harbor offers no
      run-level override for the verifier phase (resolve_verifier_phase_policy does no
      extra-host merge and there is no --allow-verifier-host flag), and allowed_hosts is
      validated as literal hostnames and never env-expanded -- so an allowlist would mean
      hardcoding the endpoint into every task. task.toml therefore declares:

          [verifier]
          network_mode = "public"

      The agent phase stays closed; its model host is injected at run time instead.

      Any failure here -- unset key, blocked egress, HTTP error, unparseable response --
      falls through to the sub-agent request below. The judge must never fail the run.

  Sub-agent (fallback, out-of-band)

  Phase 1 (during the verifier run)
      No verdict exists yet, so this writes a self-contained judge request into the judge
      dir -- criteria_payload.json, source.txt (the candidate diff), changed_files.txt (the
      FULL text of every file the diff touched), and PROMPT.md -- prints nothing, and exits 0.
      The verifier then scores on tests alone.

      What the judge deliberately does NOT get: the task instruction (a criterion that has to
      defer to the prompt is a Major "not self-contained" rubric defect -- handing the judge the
      prompt would let such a criterion pass and hide the defect), the golden solution/fix.patch
      (seeing it turns
      the judge into a similarity checker, reintroducing the very overfitting the rubric exists
      to catch), the tests/test.patch (same failure mode, and the tests already score that),
      the before/after images (UI-evaluation criteria are out of scope by definition), and
      browse access to the wider repo (unavailable at rescore time, so it would work in phase 1
      and silently not in phase 2).

  Phase 2 (after the run, orchestrated outside the container)
      A judge sub-agent reads PROMPT.md and writes verdict.json next to it. Re-running this
      script (or `mm_run.sh <task> rescore`) reads that verdict and prints "pass" or "fail".

Contract (test.sh and verifier.py depend on all four):
  * prints "pass" or "fail" on stdout, or NOTHING when no verdict is available yet.
    stdout is captured verbatim into test.sh's RUBRIC, so every diagnostic goes to stderr.
  * writes the per-criterion detail to <judge dir>/summary.json
  * writes {"failed": [...]} to /logs/verifier/rubric.json, which is the path verifier.py
    actually reads for rubric_failed_count (it previously only ever found summary.json in
    the judge dir, so that count was structurally always 0)
  * ALWAYS exits 0, so the judge can never fail the run

Env:
  EVAL_API_KEY      LiteLLM proxy key; absent => skip the API backend entirely
  EVAL_BASE_URL     OpenAI-compatible base, already ending in /v1
  EVAL_MODEL        model name as registered on the proxy
  EVAL_USER         optional; sent as the request's `user` so the proxy can attribute spend
  PB_JUDGE_DIR      where the request/verdict live (default /logs/verifier/judge)
  PB_JUDGE_VERDICT  explicit path to verdict.json (overrides the default location)

Only the stdlib is used for the HTTP call: the verifier image is node:22-bookworm with no
pip install step, so requests/httpx are not available.

IMPORTANT: never name a file in tests/ after a stdlib module (select.py, json.py, types.py,
io.py, queue.py). It shadows the real module and the failure surfaces somewhere unrelated.
The sys.path strip below defends against it.
"""
import os
import sys

_self_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path[:] = [p for p in sys.path if os.path.abspath(p or os.getcwd()) != _self_dir]

import argparse
import json
import re
import subprocess
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_JUDGE_DIR = "/logs/verifier/judge"
# verifier.py reads this exact path for rubric_failed_count.
RUBRIC_JSON_PATH = "/logs/verifier/rubric.json"
# Bounded well inside the 2400s verifier timeout even in the worst case
# (API_ATTEMPTS * API_TIMEOUT_SEC + backoff).
API_TIMEOUT_SEC = 300
API_ATTEMPTS = 3
# Hunks for these paths never reach the judge: it must grade the fix, not the harness the
# submission may have edited.
EXCLUDE_RE = re.compile(
    # Widened beyond the original JS/TS-only patterns. Measured against the corpus, the
    # old form let test files through on 13 tasks -- notably harbor's OWN generated
    # `harbor_test.js` (underscore, not `.test.js`), plus `test_*.cpp`, `*_test.go` and
    # `test_*.py`. A judge that can see the graded tests grades similarity to them, which
    # is the overfitting the rubric exists to catch.
    r"(\.test\.[jt]sx?$|\.spec\.[jt]sx?$"
    r"|_test\.(js|jsx|ts|tsx|py|go|cpp|cc|c|java|kt)$"
    r"|(^|/)test_[^/]+\.(py|cpp|cc|c)$"
    r"|(^|/)jest\.config\.[jt]s$|(^|/)vitest\.config\.[jt]s$"
    r"|(^|/)tests?/|(^|/)__tests__/|(^|/)__snapshots__/"
    r"|(^|/)node_modules/|(^|/)\.git/)"
)
BASE_REFS = ("harbor_base", "HEAD")

JUDGE_SYSTEM = (
    "You are a strict senior engineer grading the APPROACH of a code change -- not whether "
    "its tests pass. Score each rubric criterion STRICTLY BINARY: 1 = fully satisfied, "
    "0 = not satisfied. There is NO partial credit: if a criterion is only partially met, "
    "ambiguous, or has no clear evidence, score 0. Be strict; when unsure, score 0."
)


def judge_dir() -> Path:
    return Path(os.environ.get("PB_JUDGE_DIR") or DEFAULT_JUDGE_DIR)


def mark_untracked(repo: str) -> None:
    """Make files the submission ADDED visible to `git diff`.

    `git diff <ref>` reports tracked paths only, so a fix delivered as a NEW file -- a new
    stylesheet, a new module -- does not appear in it at all. The judge would then grade
    criteria about that file having never seen its contents and, under the "score 0 when
    unsure" rule, fail a correct submission. Observed on this task: the golden fix adds
    CSS/jwtHistory.css carrying every layout rule, and the two criteria that read it scored
    0 while the one criterion satisfiable from the tracked file alone scored 1.

    `add -N` (intent-to-add) records the paths in the index WITHOUT staging content, which
    is the smallest change that makes them show up as additions in the diff. Untracked
    paths that .gitignore covers stay hidden, which is what we want for build artefacts.
    """
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard"],
                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
        paths = [p for p in (out.stdout or "").splitlines() if p.strip()]
        if not paths:
            return
        add = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "add", "-N"] + paths,
                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
        if add.returncode == 0:
            sys.stderr.write("[judge] marked %d added file(s) intent-to-add so the diff "
                             "shows them: %s\n" % (len(paths), ", ".join(paths[:10])))
        else:
            sys.stderr.write("[judge] git add -N exited %d: %s\n"
                             % (add.returncode, (add.stderr or "").strip()[:300]))
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] could not mark untracked files: %s\n" % exc)


def candidate_diff(repo: str, budget: int = 120_000) -> str:
    mark_untracked(repo)
    for ref in BASE_REFS:
        try:
            out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "diff", ref],
                                 capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
        except Exception as exc:
            sys.stderr.write("[judge] git diff failed: %s\n" % exc)
            return ""
        if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
            sys.stderr.write("[judge] diffing against %s\n" % ref)
            return filter_diff(out.stdout, budget)
        # Surface WHY a ref produced nothing. A non-zero git exit here (bad ref, dubious
        # ownership, corrupt index) is indistinguishable from "the agent changed nothing"
        # unless we say so, and it silently skips rubric grading entirely.
        if out.returncode != 0:
            sys.stderr.write(
                "[judge] git diff %s exited %d: %s\n"
                % (ref, out.returncode, (out.stderr or "").strip()[:300])
            )
    sys.stderr.write("[judge] no non-empty diff found against any of %s\n"
                     % ", ".join(BASE_REFS))
    return ""


def filter_diff(diff: str, budget: int) -> str:
    kept, cur, keep = [], [], True
    for line in diff.splitlines(keepends=True):
        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
            if keep and cur:
                kept.extend(cur)
            parts = line.split()
            path = parts[-1][2:] if len(parts) >= 4 else ""
            keep = not EXCLUDE_RE.search(path)
            cur = [line]
        else:
            cur.append(line)
    if keep and cur:
        kept.extend(cur)
    blob = "".join(kept)
    return blob[:budget] + "\n[... truncated ...]\n" if len(blob) > budget else blob


def changed_paths(diff: str) -> list:
    """Paths touched by the (already harness-filtered) diff, in order."""
    out = []
    for line in diff.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) >= 4:
                p = parts[-1][2:]                  # strip the b/ prefix
                if p and p not in out:
                    out.append(p)
    return out


def collect_changed_files(repo: str, diff: str, budget: int = 200_000) -> str:
    """Full current text of every file the diff touched.

    A hunk shows three lines of context, which is often too little to decide a criterion that
    is genuinely true of the change (e.g. "the helper is defined in the same module"). Whole
    files remove that class of false 0 while staying bounded by the size of the change.
    """
    blob, used = [], 0
    for rel in changed_paths(diff):
        fp = Path(repo) / rel
        if not fp.is_file():                       # deleted or renamed away
            continue
        try:
            text = fp.read_text(errors="replace")
        except Exception:
            continue
        chunk = "\n===== %s =====\n%s" % (rel, text)
        if used + len(chunk) > budget:
            blob.append("\n[... remaining changed files omitted for length ...]\n")
            break
        blob.append(chunk); used += len(chunk)
    return "".join(blob)


def write_request(criteria, diff, jdir: Path, changed: str = "") -> None:
    """Lay down everything a judge sub-agent needs, with no further context."""
    jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    payload = [{"id": c["id"], "criterion": c["criterion"]} for c in criteria]
    (jdir / "criteria_payload.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
    (jdir / "source.txt").write_text(diff)
    extra = []
    if changed.strip():
        (jdir / "changed_files.txt").write_text(changed)
        extra.append("- `changed_files.txt` — the FULL current text of every file the diff "
                     "touched. Use it when a hunk alone is too little context to decide a "
                     "criterion.")
    extra_block = ("\n" + "\n".join(extra)) if extra else ""
    verdict = jdir / "verdict.json"
    ids = ", ".join(c["id"] for c in criteria)
    (jdir / "PROMPT.md").write_text(f"""# Rubric judge (sub-agent)

You are the rubric judge. Grade the APPROACH of a code change, not whether its tests pass.

System contract:
{JUDGE_SYSTEM}

Inputs in this directory ({jdir}):
- `criteria_payload.json` — {len(criteria)} criteria, each {{id, criterion}}.
- `source.txt` — the candidate diff. Test, spec and snapshot files are already stripped out,
  so everything you see is product code the submission changed.{extra_block}

You are NOT given the task instruction, the reference/golden fix, the tests, or the rest of the
repository. Judge only what is here. If a criterion cannot be decided from these inputs, score it 0 — but note that a
criterion which is undecidable here is a defect in the rubric, not in the submission.

Score each criterion **1 or 0 — never 0.5 or any fraction**. 1 = fully satisfied,
0 = not satisfied, ambiguous, or no clear evidence. Be strict; when unsure, score 0.

The rubric is unweighted and every criterion is mandatory: a single 0 fails the whole rubric,
so do not withhold a 1 over style preferences the criterion does not actually state.

Write ONLY this JSON to `{verdict}`:

    {{"scores": {{"<criterion id>": {{"score": 0|1}}, ...}}}}

All {len(criteria)} ids must appear: {ids}. Verify the file parses before you finish.
""")


def build_user_prompt(criteria, diff: str, changed: str) -> str:
    """The API-backend counterpart of PROMPT.md, with the same inputs and exclusions.

    Deliberately withheld, exactly as in the sub-agent request: the task instruction, the
    golden fix.patch, tests/test.patch, and the screenshots. See the module docstring for
    why each one would corrupt the grade.
    """
    payload = json.dumps(
        [{"id": c["id"], "criterion": c["criterion"]} for c in criteria], indent=2
    )
    ids = ", ".join(c["id"] for c in criteria)
    parts = [
        "Grade the APPROACH of the code change below against each rubric criterion.",
        "",
        "## Criteria",
        payload,
        "",
        "## Candidate diff (test/spec/snapshot files already stripped)",
        "```diff",
        diff,
        "```",
    ]
    if changed.strip():
        parts += [
            "",
            "## Full current text of every file the diff touched",
            "Use this when a hunk alone is too little context to decide a criterion.",
            changed,
        ]
    parts += [
        "",
        "## Output",
        'Reply with JSON only, no prose and no code fences: {"scores": {"<id>": 0 or 1}}.',
        f"All {len(criteria)} ids must be present: {ids}.",
        "Score 1 only when the criterion is fully satisfied with clear evidence in the "
        "change; otherwise score 0. There is no partial credit.",
    ]
    return "\n".join(parts)


def extract_scores_object(text: str):
    """Parse the model reply into a dict, tolerating fences and surrounding prose."""
    candidate = text.strip()
    if candidate.startswith("```"):
        candidate = re.sub(r"^```[a-zA-Z]*\n?", "", candidate)
        candidate = re.sub(r"\n?```$", "", candidate.strip())
    try:
        return json.loads(candidate)
    except Exception:
        pass
    start, depth = None, 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(candidate):
        if ch == "{":
            if start is None:
                start = i
            depth += 1
        elif ch == "}" and start is not None:
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                try:
                    return json.loads(candidate[start : i + 1])
                except Exception:
                    start, depth = None, 0
    return None


def call_eval_api(criteria, diff: str, changed: str):
    """Grade via the proxy. Returns a scores-shaped dict, or None to fall back.

    Never raises: every failure path returns None so the caller can fall through to the
    sub-agent request and the run is never failed by the judge.
    """
    api_key = (os.environ.get("EVAL_API_KEY") or "").strip()
    base_url = (os.environ.get("EVAL_BASE_URL") or "").strip().rstrip("/")
    model = (os.environ.get("EVAL_MODEL") or "").strip()
    if not api_key or not base_url or not model:
        sys.stderr.write(
            "[judge] API backend unavailable (EVAL_API_KEY/EVAL_BASE_URL/EVAL_MODEL "
            "incomplete); falling back to the sub-agent request\n"
        )
        return None

    body = {
        "model": model,
        "temperature": 0,
        "messages": [
            {"role": "system", "content": JUDGE_SYSTEM},
            {"role": "user", "content": build_user_prompt(criteria, diff, changed)},
        ],
    }
    # The proxy attributes spend per `user`; without it this call is unattributable.
    if os.environ.get("EVAL_USER"):
        body["user"] = os.environ["EVAL_USER"]

    url = base_url + "/chat/completions"
    data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
    for attempt in range(1, API_ATTEMPTS + 1):
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(
                url,
                data=data,
                method="POST",
                headers={
                    "Authorization": "Bearer %s" % api_key,
                    "Content-Type": "application/json",
                },
            )
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=API_TIMEOUT_SEC) as resp:
                raw = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            content = json.loads(raw)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
            obj = extract_scores_object(content)
            if not isinstance(obj, dict):
                sys.stderr.write(
                    "[judge] attempt %d: reply was not JSON: %r\n" % (attempt, content[:400])
                )
            else:
                sys.stderr.write("[judge] graded via API model=%s\n" % model)
                return obj
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            detail = ""
            try:
                detail = exc.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")[:400]
            except Exception:
                pass
            sys.stderr.write(
                "[judge] attempt %d: HTTP %s %s\n" % (attempt, exc.code, detail)
            )
            # 4xx other than 429 will not fix themselves; stop retrying.
            if 400 <= exc.code < 500 and exc.code != 429:
                break
        except Exception as exc:
            sys.stderr.write(
                "[judge] attempt %d: %s: %s\n" % (attempt, exc.__class__.__name__, exc)
            )
        if attempt < API_ATTEMPTS:
            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
    sys.stderr.write("[judge] API backend gave up; falling back to the sub-agent request\n")
    return None


def write_rubric_json(failed, total: int) -> None:
    """verifier.py reads this for rubric_failed_count."""
    try:
        Path(RUBRIC_JSON_PATH).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with open(RUBRIC_JSON_PATH, "w") as handle:
            json.dump({"failed": list(failed), "criteria_total": total}, handle, indent=2)
    except OSError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] could not write %s: %s\n" % (RUBRIC_JSON_PATH, exc))


def read_verdict(criteria, jdir: Path):
    """Return ("pass"|"fail", failed_ids) or None when no usable verdict exists."""
    vp = Path(os.environ.get("PB_JUDGE_VERDICT") or (jdir / "verdict.json"))
    if not vp.is_file():
        return None
    try:
        obj = json.loads(vp.read_text())
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict unreadable (%s)\n" % exc)
        return None
    scores = obj.get("scores", obj)
    if not isinstance(scores, dict):
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict has no scores map\n")
        return None
    failed, graded = [], 0
    for c in criteria:
        raw = scores.get(c["id"])
        if raw is None:
            failed.append(c["id"])            # not graded == not demonstrated == fail
            continue
        try:
            v = float(raw.get("score") if isinstance(raw, dict) else raw)
        except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            failed.append(c["id"])
            continue
        graded += 1
        if v < 1.0:                            # strictly binary: only a full 1 passes
            failed.append(c["id"])
    if graded == 0:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict contained no usable scores\n")
        return None
    return ("fail" if failed else "pass"), failed


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--rubrics", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--repo", default="/app")
    ap.add_argument("--judge-dir", default=None)
    a = ap.parse_args()

    jdir = Path(a.judge_dir) if a.judge_dir else judge_dir()
    try:
        doc = json.load(open(a.rubrics))
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] cannot read %s: %s\n" % (a.rubrics, exc))
        return 0
    criteria = [c for c in (doc.get("criteria") or []) if c.get("id") and c.get("criterion")]
    if not criteria:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] no criteria in %s\n" % a.rubrics)
        return 0

    def emit(verdict, failed) -> int:
        """Publish a verdict: summary.json, rubric.json, then stdout LAST."""
        try:
            jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            json.dump({"rubric": verdict, "failed": failed,
                       "criteria_total": len(criteria)},
                      open(jdir / "summary.json", "w"), indent=2)
        except Exception:
            pass
        write_rubric_json(failed, len(criteria))
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict=%s%s\n"
                         % (verdict, (" failed=%s" % ", ".join(failed)) if failed else ""))
        print(verdict)
        return 0

    # An existing verdict.json always wins: it is either a sub-agent verdict or this
    # script's own API result being rescored, and re-grading would cost a second call.
    res = read_verdict(criteria, jdir)
    if res is not None:
        return emit(*res)

    diff = candidate_diff(a.repo)
    if not diff.strip():
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] empty candidate diff; nothing to grade\n")
        return 0
    changed = collect_changed_files(a.repo, diff)

    # Preferred: grade in-band via the proxy. Persist the scores as verdict.json so the
    # grade is auditable and a rescore is idempotent, then score it through read_verdict
    # so both backends share one scoring path.
    scores = call_eval_api(criteria, diff, changed)
    if scores is not None:
        try:
            jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            (jdir / "verdict.json").write_text(json.dumps(scores, indent=2))
        except OSError as exc:
            sys.stderr.write("[judge] could not persist verdict.json: %s\n" % exc)
        res = read_verdict(criteria, jdir)
        if res is not None:
            return emit(*res)
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] API verdict had no usable scores; writing the request\n")

    # Fallback: lay down the sub-agent request and stay silent.
    write_request(criteria, diff, jdir, changed=changed)
    sys.stderr.write(
        "[judge] no verdict at %s yet; wrote the judge request to %s (%s). Have the judge "
        "sub-agent produce verdict.json, then rescore. Scoring on tests alone until then.\n"
        % (jdir / "verdict.json", jdir, ", ".join(sorted(f.name for f in jdir.iterdir()))))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
